questions.question: How does software security primarily differ from software quality and reliability?
options: Quality deals with intentional attacks while security focuses on accidental failures.
Security addresses the probability distribution of random, unanticipated inputs.
Security focuses on intentional attacks where the attacker chooses the input distribution.
Reliability uses structured design while security relies solely on perimeter defenses.
questions.answer: Security focuses on intentional attacks where the attacker chooses the input distribution.

questions.question: What is the core rule of defensive programming?
options: Always use the most complex algorithm available to confuse attackers.
Never assume anything and check all assumptions and potential error states.
Rely on the operating system to handle all resource management issues.
Filter all input through a centralized firewall before it reaches the application.
questions.answer: Never assume anything and check all assumptions and potential error states.

questions.question: Which attack occurs when input data is used to construct a system command executed with the privileges of the web server?
options: Command injection
Cross-site request forgery
Memory leak exploitation
Buffer over-read
questions.answer: Command injection

questions.question: What process replaces multiple, alternative encodings of data with a single, standard representation before validation?
options: Fuzzing
Canonicalization
Static linking
Privilege escalation
questions.answer: Canonicalization

questions.question: Which software testing technique provides random or semi-random data to find security or reliability flaws?
options: Formal methods
Regression testing
Fuzzing
Atomic synchronization
questions.answer: Fuzzing

questions.question: What is a memory leak?
options: An unauthorized access to sensitive data stored in the process heap.
A failure to release dynamic memory, potentially leading to denial-of-service.
A bug where an attacker can read the contents of adjacent memory blocks.
A race condition where two threads overwrite the same memory location.
questions.answer: A failure to release dynamic memory, potentially leading to denial-of-service.

questions.question: In the context of concurrent execution, what is a race condition?
options: A situation where multiple processes compete for a single CPU core.
An attack that uses predictable TCP sequence numbers to hijack a session.
The steady reduction of available system memory due to poor management.
A situation where output depends on the sequence or timing of uncontrollable events.
questions.answer: A situation where output depends on the sequence or timing of uncontrollable events.

questions.question: What is an atomic operation?
options: An operation treated as a single, uninterruptible unit of execution.
A low-level machine instruction that interacts directly with hardware.
A cryptographic function used to generate unpredictable random seeds.
A script that runs with the highest possible system privileges.
questions.answer: An operation treated as a single, uninterruptible unit of execution.

questions.question: Why is allowlisting generally considered more secure than denylisting for input validation?
options: Denylisting requires significantly more processing power and memory.
Allowlisting handles new, undiscovered attack encodings by only accepting known safe data.
Denylisting is impossible to implement using standard regular expressions.
Allowlisting automatically performs canonicalization on all incoming data.
questions.answer: Allowlisting handles new, undiscovered attack encodings by only accepting known safe data.

questions.question: A web application displays user comments to other visitors. What is the primary risk if this output is not sanitized?
options: SQL injection in the backend database.
Command injection on the web server OS.
Cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks on other users' browsers.
Privilege escalation of the guestbook service account.
questions.answer: Cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks on other users' browsers.

questions.question: How does the principle of least privilege improve software security?
options: It prevents attackers from discovering bugs in the algorithm implementation.
It ensures that a compromised program has minimal access to the rest of the system.
It eliminates the need for input validation by restricting user capabilities.
It forces all programs to use static linking for their standard libraries.
questions.answer: It ensures that a compromised program has minimal access to the rest of the system.

questions.question: Which environment variable flaw allows an attacker to trick a shell script into executing a malicious program by placing it in a controlled directory?
options: Manipulating the IFS variable to change word boundaries.
Modifying the PATH variable to point to the attacker's directory.
Changing LD_LIBRARY_PATH to load a custom version of a standard library.
Overwriting the REPLYTO variable to redirect system emails.
questions.answer: Modifying the PATH variable to point to the attacker's directory.

questions.question: Why did the 2014 Heartbleed vulnerability occur in OpenSSL?
options: A failure to validate the length of a requested data return in a binary protocol.
An insecure random number seed that made session keys predictable.
A race condition between two threads accessing the same SSL certificate.
The use of shell metacharacters in a web form that allowed remote execution.
questions.answer: A failure to validate the length of a requested data return in a binary protocol.

questions.question: What is the security risk associated with using symbolic links when creating temporary files?
options: The link could bypass the chroot jail by pointing to an external directory.
An attacker could redirect a privileged write to a critical system file like /etc/passwd.
The symbolic link consumes excessive disk space, leading to a denial-of-service.
Symbolic links prevent the operating system from using atomic creation primitives.
questions.answer: An attacker could redirect a privileged write to a critical system file like /etc/passwd.

questions.question: When developing a secure file shredder, why is application-level flushing of buffers insufficient?
options: The operating system also maintains a file handling buffer that reorders writes.
Application buffers only store metadata and not the actual bit patterns.
The standard C library automatically ignores flush requests for small files.
Flushing buffers only works for magnetic disks and not flash memory drives.
questions.answer: The operating system also maintains a file handling buffer that reorders writes.

questions.question: How can a developer safely use a privileged shell script on a Unix system?
options: By always setting the script to run as the root user.
By using a compiled wrapper program to construct a safe environment before execution.
By ensuring that the script uses relative paths for all system utilities.
By disabling all environment variables globally for the entire system.
questions.answer: By using a compiled wrapper program to construct a safe environment before execution.

questions.question: An attacker provides the input 'Bob'; drop table suppliers' to a web form. Which mitigation specifically addresses this attack?
options: Using mkstemp() for all database interaction files.
Implementing the sticky bit on the database directory.
Using SQL placeholders or parameters to securely build statements.
Restricting the PATH variable of the database service.
questions.answer: Using SQL placeholders or parameters to securely build statements.

questions.question: A programmer uses a loop to check if a lockfile exists and then creates it if it is missing. Why is this vulnerable?
options: The check and creation are not atomic, allowing a race condition.
Lockfiles are advisory and can be ignored by any malicious process.
The loop may fail if the filesystem uses a journaling mechanism.
The process ID used in the lockfile can be guessed by the attacker.
questions.answer: The check and creation are not atomic, allowing a race condition.

questions.question: A developer wants to prevent XSS reflection on a site that allows users to post HTML formatting. What is the most secure approach?
options: Denylist the <script> tag while allowing all other HTML tags.
Use an anti-XSS library that only allows a strictly validated set of safe markup.
Translate all Unicode input to ASCII before displaying it to other users.
Ensure the web server runs with the least possible privileges on the OS.
questions.answer: Use an anti-XSS library that only allows a strictly validated set of safe markup.

questions.question: A C program accepts an unsigned integer for buffer size and compares it to a maximum limit. If the code later casts this value to a signed integer during a bounds check, what exploit becomes possible?
options: A command injection using shell metacharacters.
A buffer overflow caused by a large positive value being treated as negative.
A memory leak that exhausts the process heap over time.
A race condition where the comparison is bypassed by a separate thread.
questions.answer: A buffer overflow caused by a large positive value being treated as negative.
